script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Ever wondered about getting rewards without putting in the work? Let's dive into today's idiom! [break 1s] The phrase is: 不劳而获 (bù láo ér huò) [break 1s] 不 (bù) - not [break 0.5s] 劳 (láo) - labor [break 0.5s] 而 (ér) - and [break 0.5s] 获 (huò) - to gain [break 0.5s] Full idiom again: 不劳而获 means literally 'not labor and gain' and figuratively refers to gaining without effort. [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] This idiom originates from ancient Chinese texts where it was stated that one cannot expect to harvest crops without first toiling the land. It reflects the idea that effort is necessary to achieve success, and nothing worthwhile comes without hard work. Over time, this phrase has been used to caution against laziness and unrealistic expectations in life. [break 1.5s] Three examples: [break 1s] 他想不劳而获，结果失去了所有。 [break 1s] He wanted to gain without effort and ended up losing everything. [break 1s] 不要期望不劳而获，努力工作才是成功的关键。 [break 1s] Don't expect to gain without effort; hard work is the key to success. [break 1s] 这样的想法只会让你不劳而获。 [break 1s] Such thinking will only lead you to expect rewards without effort. [break 1s] So remember, 不劳而获 means gaining without effort. Thank you for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom. [break 1s]
